instruction: Make the title on slide 2 bold and change its font color to red.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated to slide 2, selected the title 'Product Comparison', and moved it to the bottom of the slide in 16 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate between slides, select text boxes, edit text, move shapes by position in LibreOffice Impress.
metadata.task_rationale: The model can select and manipulate slide titles. This variation tests formatting capabilities (bold + color) instead of repositioning.
metadata.explanation: Task requires making slide 2 title bold and changing its font color to red. Evaluator reads title font properties and checks bold=True (0.5) and color=FF0000 (0.5) for partial credit.

llm_judge_reasons: Metric correctly handles rule-type expected parameter: directly accesses expected.get('expected_bold') and expected.get('expected_color_rgb') without wrapping in 'rules' key.
Both instruction requirements (bold + red font color) are verified with appropriate partial credit scoring (0.5 each).
Postconfig correctly saves the file with Ctrl+S before getter reads it, ensuring state freshness.
Getter uses slide_index=1 (0-based) which correctly targets slide 2.

CONCERN: Getter identifies the title placeholder by checking 'PlaceHolder 1' in shape.name. In many PPTX templates, title placeholders are named 'Title 1' rather than 'PlaceHolder 1'. This could cause the getter to fail to find the title and return an error. A more robust approach would use shape.placeholder_format with idx=0 or check for PP_PLACEHOLDER.TITLE.

MINOR: Getter only examines the first run of the first paragraph. If the title has multiple runs with inconsistent formatting, the check could miss partial formatting. However, for a uniform bold+color change this is generally acceptable.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Replace the placeholder name check ('PlaceHolder 1' in shape.name) with a more robust approach: use shape.placeholder_format to check if the shape is a title placeholder (idx == 0), or iterate all placeholders and check shape.placeholder_format.type.
Consider checking all runs in the title text frame to ensure uniform formatting, rather than only the first run of the first paragraph.
